channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Chip Roy, Mayes Middleton leading Texas attorney general GOP primary in new poll
item.description: The poll, released Wednesday, also showed Sid Miller and Don Huffines with comfortable leads in their Republican primary bids for agriculture commissioner and comptroller.

item.title: The week in politics (Feb. 11, 2026)
item.description: On Wednesday's show: We discuss the latest developments in politics in our weekly roundup. And we visit a new farmer-owned grocery store in Sunnyside.

item.title: FAA lifts airspace restriction in El Paso as Transportation Secretary blames ‘cartel drone incursion’
item.description: All flights to and from El Paso and Santa Teresa were prohibited under a temporary flight restriction issued Tuesday night by the Federal Aviation Administration.

item.title: Trump administration is sending pregnant migrant girls to South Texas shelter flagged as medically inadequate
item.description: Government sources and advocates for the children worry the goal is to concentrate them in Texas, where abortion is banned.

item.title: Houston officials seek input from tenants and landlords about proposed apartment inspection ordinance
item.description: The Houston City Council is considering adopting rules that would create a registry of “high-risk rental buildings” based on repeated health and safety violations.

item.title: Nearly 80% of Houstonians worry about the cost of living outpacing wages, survey finds
item.description: A survey published by the University of Houston Hobby School of Public Affairs collected responses from residents of Houston and Chicago to gauge the economic perceptions of those living in the nation’s third- and fourth-largest cities.

item.title: Hello Houston (February 11, 2026)
item.description: Today: We discuss a University of Houston report concerning Texas’s new school vouchers program, Nate Sheets talks about his run for Texas Agriculture Commissioner, and we explore the traditions of Lunar New Year.

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (February 11, 2026)
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters, we have – The Commuter Cut – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: Texas launches $13 million statewide spay, neuter, vaccination program
item.description: The funds will be distributed to municipal and county shelters, private animal shelters, 501(c) nonprofits, animal rescue entities, and veterinary clinics across Texas that apply for direct grants ranging from $50,000 to $500,000 per fiscal year.

item.title: Harris County seeks restraining order against federal government to halt FEMA layoffs
item.description: The filing -- part of a lawsuit filed in the Northern District of California with other government agencies last year -- seeks an order that would restrict the Department of Homeland Security's ability to direct sweeping layoffs in the emergency management agency.
